decisions.claim: B has a screen near the steering wheel in B's vehicle
decisions.reason: Definite description 'the screen near your steering wheel' presupposes existence of a screen near B's steering wheel.

decisions.claim: B has a steering wheel (implying B has a vehicle)
decisions.reason: Possessive 'your steering wheel' presupposes B has a steering wheel (and thus a vehicle).

decisions.claim: B's screen/TV is on every day
decisions.reason: Question 'what's on everyday' presupposes the screen/TV is on every day; the question asks about content, not whether it is on.

decisions.claim: B has a TV (the screen is referred to as a TV)
decisions.reason: A uses definite 'the TV' referring back to the screen; this is A's labeling of the screen as a TV, a presupposition from context.

decisions.claim: B pays for the programs on the TV
decisions.reason: 'Do you pay for the programs?' is a yes/no question; it does NOT presuppose B pays. Questions do not establish their answers.
decisions.counterexample: B might not pay for programs; A is simply asking.

decisions.claim: B has passengers in B's vehicle
decisions.reason: Definite possessive 'your passengers' presupposes B has passengers.

decisions.claim: A is one of B's passengers
decisions.reason: 'your passengers like me' explicitly states A is one of B's passengers via coreference.

decisions.claim: The TV can entertain B's passengers
decisions.reason: Explicit statement: 'It can also entertain your passengers like me' – A asserts the TV's capability.

decisions.claim: B has a steering wheel (is driving a vehicle)
decisions.reason: Same claim as c2 (B has a steering wheel/vehicle); c2 is the more precise E1 presupposition from the definite possessive.

decisions.claim: B has a screen near the steering wheel in their vehicle
decisions.reason: Same claim as c1 (B has a screen near the steering wheel); c1 is the E1 definite-description presupposition.

decisions.claim: B's screen is referred to as a TV by A
decisions.reason: Same claim as c4 (the screen is referred to as a TV); c4 already captures this.

decisions.claim: B has passengers in their vehicle
decisions.reason: Same claim as c6 (B has passengers); c6 is the E1 presupposition from 'your passengers'.

decisions.claim: A is a passenger in B's vehicle
decisions.reason: A explicitly states 'your passengers like me' in turn 15, directly presupposing A's role as a passenger in B's vehicle. This is a solid E2 presupposition from A's own words.

decisions.claim: The programs on B's TV are somewhat expensive but considered worth the cost
decisions.reason: Turn 13 is A's own statement/opinion about the programs being expensive but worth it. This is A's evaluative comment, not an established attribute of B. A's opinion about the cost does not constitute a fact about B's property or experience.
decisions.counterexample: A could be making a general comment or hypothetical rather than reporting B's actual experience with the programs.
